questions.prompt: A sound wave in air has a wavelength of 0.85 m and speed 340 m/s. What is its frequency?
Two notes have frequencies of 256 Hz and 512 Hz. How does the second compare with the first?
options: Higher pitch and half the wavelength
Lower pitch and the same wavelength
questions.explain: Double the frequency: higher pitch; same speed, so half the wavelength.

questions.prompt: A person hears the echo of a shout 3 s after shouting towards a cliff. How far away is the cliff? (v = 340 m/s)
Which is a use of ultrasound?
options: Heating food in a microwave oven
questions.explain: Echoes from a crack reveal flaws that can’t be seen.

questions.prompt: What is the time period of a sound wave with a frequency of 100 Hz?
Why does thunder reach you after the lightning flash?
options: Thunder is made later than the lightning
Light travels far faster than sound
questions.explain: Light arrives almost instantly; sound takes about 3 s per kilometre.

questions.prompt: You see lightning and hear the thunder 6 s later. About how far away is the storm? (v = 340 m/s)
questions.explain: d = v × t = 340 × 6 = 2040 m (no halving: the sound travels one way).

questions.prompt: A student says, "Sound is air travelling from the speaker to your ear." Correct this statement using the idea of a longitudinal wave.
questions.modelAnswer: Sound is not air travelling; it is energy travelling as a longitudinal wave. The speaker cone vibrates and pushes the neighbouring air particles, creating compressions and rarefactions. Each particle only vibrates back and forth about its own position, passing the vibration to the next particles, so the pattern (and energy) travels to your ear while the air stays in place on average.
